DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OILG OPINION NO. 03 HON. ROSALINA G. JALOSJOS Governor Province of Zamboanga del Norte Office of the Governor Provincial Capitol Gen. Luna St., Brgy. Estaka, Dipolog City HON. CECILIA J. CARREON Mayor Municipality of Pifian, Province of Zamboanga del Norte Dear Govemor Jalosjos and Mayor Carreon: This refers to the letter dated August 29, 2024 from the Honorable Governor of the Province of Zamboanga del Norte, in relation to the letter of the Honorable Mayor of the Municipality of Pifian, seeking for this Department's guidance pertaining to Resolution No. 710, series of 2024 passed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Zamboanga del Norte entitled "A RESOLUTION IMPOSING A 60-DAY PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION WITHOUT PAY TO MUNICIPAL MAYOR CECILIA J. CARREON OF ANAN, ZAMBOANGA DEL NORTE, RESPONDENT IN ADMINISTRATIVE CASE NO. 2023- 03, TO PREVENT INTERFERENCE IN THE INVESTIGATION OF THE SUBJECT CASE". Both letters presented the following facts: • The Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP), as contained in Resolution No. 710, directed the Provincial Governor, to implement a 60-day suspension on Respondent Mayor Cecilia J. Carreon. The Provincial Govemor received a copy of Respondent's Motion for Reconsideration which prayed that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan should reconsider its order alleging that the Resolution did not comply with the legal requirements for the imposition of preventive suspension citing Section 63 (a) and (b) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC). Gov. Rosalina Jalosjos claims that in the exercise of the authority to implement the preventive suspension, she, as the Provincial Govemor, is duty bound to Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

determine if the requisites are present. Therefore, it is imperative on the part of the provincial governor to determine if any of the grounds enumerated in Section 63 of the LGC are present in the exercise of her discretion. • On August 21, 2024, Gov. Jalosjos issued an Order voluntarily inhibiting the implementation of Resolution No. 710 in the spirit of partiality and fairness considering that the respondent is her sister. Under the premise of Gov. Jalosjos' inhibition arose the request for clarification on the following matters: 1. Considering the inhibition of the provincial govemor, who now has the authority to Act No. Resolution No. 710? 2. Given the inhibition, is it proper and more prudent for the Office of the Govemor to forward the Resolution No. 710 to the Office of the President for proper action? Section 63 (a) and (b) of the LGC provides to wit: SECTION 63. Preventive Suspension. — (a) Preventive suspension may be imposed: (I) xxx (2) By the governor, if the respondent is an elective official of a component city or municipality; or (3) xxx (b) Preventive suspension may be imposed at any time after the issues are joined, when the evidence of guilt is strong, and given the gravity of the offense, there is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence: Provided, That, any single preventive suspension of local elective officials shall not extend beyond sixty (60) days: Provided, further, That in the event that several administrative cases are filed against an elective official, he cannot be preventively suspended for more than ninety (90) days within a single year on the same ground or grounds existing and known at the time of the first suspension. The said provision used the word "may" which, to our mind, gives to the concemed Local Chief Executive the discretion on whether to implement the preventive suspension issued by the Sanggunian against the elective official who has a pending case before them. It is our position that the legislative used the word "may" instead of mandatory word "shall" and the word "impose" instead of "implement" intending it to grant the local chief executive, the Governor in this case, the discretion in implementing the preventive Page 2 of 3

suspension considering that it is the governor who exercises supervision over its component local government units including its elective officials. With this, the Governor is given the authority to verify if the requirements under Section 63(b) are present before the preventive suspension is implemented. Now going to the queries and considering that they are interrelated, we will answer them jointly. The provincial governor, having inhibited herself in implementing the preventive suspension, we are of the opinion that the Resolution of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan should be fonuarded to the Office of the President for their appropriate action pursuant to the exercise of general supervision of the Office of the President over the provinces. This opinion is rendered based on the facts narrated and as appreciated by this Department without prejudice to the ruling and/or opinion of other competent authorities. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY TH ITY OF THE SECRETARY: R. LLAMAS N VIC Unders etary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs cc: PAISAL O. ABUTAZIL, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG Region IX Page 3 of 3
